name: Hue Hunt
hook: See a color for 3 seconds, then rebuild it from memory. A daily puzzle with a Wordle-style result grid.
highlights: Perceptual scoring with CIEDE2000 in Lab space, not RGB distance
Seeded daily puzzle shared by client and server; the server recomputes scores from raw guesses
Keyboard-operable 2D color picker and a canvas-rendered share card

caseStudy.problem: Make a daily game that is quick, fair and shareable.
caseStudy.architecture: A plain-ESM core (seeded RNG, color math, scoring) imported by both the React app and the Node server. The client submits guesses, never scores. node:sqlite stores submissions with one row per player per day.
decisions: The server recomputes every score from the raw guesses, so a submitted score can’t be tampered with
ΔE2000 maps to a 0-100 score that matches how different two colors look to people
The static demo swaps the HTTP adapter for a local one that fakes percentiles from a seeded distribution

name: Ghostwriter
hook: Write something, then share a link that plays it back keystroke by keystroke, typos and hesitations included.
highlights: Event-sourced document: the text is a fold over a keystroke log
Compact binary encoding + CompressionStream + base64url fits a replay in the URL
Snapshot checkpoints make seeking fast instead of replaying from zero

caseStudy.problem: Show how a text was written, not just the result, without a server ever seeing the content.
caseStudy.architecture: The editor records insert/delete events with relative timestamps. A codec delta-encodes and deflates them into the URL hash. The player rebuilds state from periodic snapshots for scrubbing.
decisions: Deliberately serverless: the link is the product and the content never leaves the URL
Varint delta encoding before compression keeps most replays under the URL comfort zone
Live region announces playback state, not every character

name: Fair Share
hook: Paste the receipt, send one link, everyone taps what they ate, and tax and tip settle themselves in real time.
highlights: Integer cents with largest-remainder allocation, so totals reconcile to the penny
WebSocket sync with versioned patches, optimistic updates and gap recovery
Static demo syncs between tabs with BroadcastChannel, no server needed

caseStudy.problem: Splitting a group bill is error-prone and nobody wants to install an app at the table.
caseStudy.architecture: A pure split function (bill, claims) → per-person totals, shared by client and server. Node + ws broadcasts versioned patches; clients request a snapshot when they detect a version gap.
decisions: Money is never a float: all math is integer cents
No accounts: each participant gets a secret token, and claims are authenticated against it
The same UI runs on a BroadcastChannel adapter for the static demo

name: Seed Sequencer
hook: A garden where every plant is a loop. Plant seeds, prune leaves, and share the song as a link.
highlights: Look-ahead scheduler on the AudioContext clock, so timer jitter never reaches the audio
Undo/redo through a command stack that merges slider drags
A full garden packs into at most about 220 URL characters

caseStudy.problem: Make music creation instant and impossible to get wrong, and make sharing a song as easy as sharing a link.
caseStudy.architecture: Vue 3 + Pinia hold the garden; a scheduler queues notes 120 ms ahead on the audio timeline and a rAF loop maps the audio clock back to the UI so plants sway exactly on their notes.
decisions: Everything is quantized to a pentatonic scale, so random input still sounds good
Synthesized voices and a generated reverb impulse: zero audio files
Roving-tabindex grids and aria-pressed toggles; motion is off under reduced motion while audio keeps playing

name: Throttle Lab
hook: Fire requests at four rate-limiting algorithms side by side and see exactly why the fifth request gets a 429.
highlights: A dependency-free Node rate-limiting library with pluggable memory and SQLite stores
The same algorithm code drives the in-browser visualization on a simulated clock
Click any denied request for a plain-English explanation of why

caseStudy.problem: Rate-limiting trade-offs are usually explained with static diagrams that hide the edge cases.
caseStudy.architecture: Algorithms are pure step functions over JSON state, so the library, the demo server and the browser share one implementation. Web Components render each lane on canvas.
decisions: Injectable clock makes every algorithm deterministic and testable
No framework on the frontend, on purpose
Standard RateLimit-* and Retry-After headers on the real server

name: Hot Take Court
hook: Submit your hottest take, let the internet be the jury, and get a verdict card: guilty of being wrong, or acquitted.
highlights: Framework-free PHP: front controller, router, controllers, repositories, PDO prepared statements
One vote per user per case enforced by a database primary key, with counters updated in the same transaction
Verdict cards render as SVG in-page and as PNG for link previews

caseStudy.problem: Opinions are fun to argue about, and a verdict card gives each argument something worth sharing.
caseStudy.architecture: Server-rendered PHP 8 with session auth, CSRF tokens and rate limiting; MySQL schema with a SQLite twin for local runs. The static demo reimplements the rules on localStorage behind the same API shape.
decisions: Constraints live in the database, not just in PHP
Trending ranks recent votes with time decay; cases close after 72 hours
Verdict share links in the demo embed a snapshot, so they work without a server
